subject: Democracy and putting power back in public hands
posts:
Civic participation is more than casting an occasional ballot while party machines pull the strings.
Evidence: Free elections, Factional pre-selection, Public alienation
#Democracy #Australia

David Higginbottom argues that true democracy requires citizens to wield genuine power over governing institutions, not just vote on pre-packaged candidates.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.6) — Good Preference

While Australian elections are free and fair, candidate selection remains locked inside insular party factions, leaving voters with managed choices rather than real power.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.5, +0.3) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Awakening.
Deep structural critique exposes how party patronage limits genuine public agency.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.3, z: 1)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Higginbottom Critique: PASS (+0.7, +0.5) — Sharp analysis of party pre-selection.
- Electoral System: COND (+0.3, +0.1) — Fair voting, closed candidate pools.
David Higginbottom examines Australian democracy, questioning how much control citizens truly exercise when candidate lists are controlled by party insiders.

The Bright Side:
Open public dialogue about systemic flaws ensures democratic institutions face necessary pressure for genuine reform.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing procedural mechanics (WHO votes) with structural power (WHO chooses candidates). Citizens pick from pre-vetted menus.

Social Physics Analysis:
Party machines run a smart selfish maneuver by hoarding candidate selection behind closed doors while projecting public consultation outward.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map the gap between procedural voting and real power, it plots a direct trajectory toward Awakening.
Systemic tension drives reform.

The Unavoidable Truth: Free elections matter little if citizens are barred from choosing candidates.

The Unavoidable Lie: Voting alone equates to genuine public self-governance.

Alethekanon:
True democratic health demands dismantling opaque factional gatekeeping. Procedural comfort must never mask structural disenfranchisement.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to feel like your voice only matters on election day while the real decisions are locked away in backrooms you can't enter.

Brothekanon:
Spot on. You get to vote, sure, but only for the two guys the party bosses already picked out for you. That's not much of a choice.

Spirithekanon:
"Hate evil, love good; maintain justice in the courts." Amos 5:15 PASS
Seeking true justice in civic structures requires aligning public power with moral integrity rather than factional control.
